key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish interface- versus bulk-dominated degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but accelerates depth-spreading recombination losses under thermal aging.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical diagnostic for designing more stable perovskite device stacks by localizing where degradation begins and how it propagates during stress testing.
method: Multiwavelength excitation PL to probe depth-sensitive recombination.
Phenethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (PEABF4) used as an interface-treatment case study.
Diffusion-recombination simulations used to interpret PL decay in terms of surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PL showed reduced interfacial recombination after PEABF4 treatment, but after thermal aging the recombination losses broadened from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with simulation results.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation depends on model assumptions and excitation penetration behavior, so it should be validated alongside complementary structural or electrical measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
